scope: Technical architecture, local operating guidance, traceability, implementation notes, and known limitations for the Windows-only Sandwich Download Manager v0.1. This record does not authorize distribution, signing, deployment, production credentials, or production data.

architecture.boundaryRule: URL validation, filename sanitisation, collision resolution, transfer segmentation, Range fallback, manifest validation, and transfer metrics belong to the Rust download-engine crate. Tauri commands and webview code consume those rules and own only desktop integration and presentation.
runtimeFlow: Manual URL submission and a confirmed clipboard offer enter the same Tauri submit_url command.
submit_url invokes shared URL and filename validation, selects an optional extension subfolder, queues a snapshot, and starts the shared engine asynchronously.
The engine probes with bytes=0-0, uses up to eight Range segments after a valid 206 response, or uses one stream when Range is ignored.
The engine writes a sidecar manifest and a .sandwich-part file, persists completed segment offsets, validates total length, atomically renames the partial file, and only then records completed.
Completed paths are passed to Tauri opener APIs only after the desktop state confirms completed status.

operatorRunbook.supportedEnvironment: Local or CI Windows development with Node.js, npm, Rust, Cargo, the Windows C++ build tools, and the Tauri/WebView2 prerequisites. Production is not authorized.
operatorRunbook.checkBehavior: Runs Node frontend tests, cargo fmt --check for the engine, locked engine runtime tests, and a locked cargo check of the Tauri desktop crate.
operatorRunbook.buildBehavior: Runs the same checks and then a locked debug cargo build of the Tauri desktop crate. It does not create, sign, publish, or deploy MSI/NSIS installers.
operatorRunbook.developmentLaunchWarning: This is an interactive foreground command for a developer terminal; automation must not use it as a verification command without detached startup, readiness polling, and explicit shutdown.
recovery: Do not rename a .sandwich-part file to a completed filename manually.
Preserve the .sandwich.json manifest and matching partial file together before troubleshooting.
load_manifest changes an active record found after restart to recoverably_interrupted while retaining segment offsets.
Use backup_manifest before changing a manifest and restore_manifest only from a successfully validated backup.
Treat malformed manifests, mismatched file length, inconsistent Range responses, or filesystem errors as failures requiring inspection; never force completed status.

incidentTriage.expected: The probe returns 200 and the engine downloads through a single segment.
incidentTriage.escalateWhen: The resulting bytes differ or the transfer fails instead of falling back.

incidentTriage.expected: A persisted manifest and partial file remain for recovery analysis.
incidentTriage.escalateWhen: The application reports completed or the partial data is exposed as final.

incidentTriage.expected: The shared collision rule selects name (n).ext without overwriting.
incidentTriage.escalateWhen: An existing file changes or output escapes the selected destination.

incidentTriage.expected: No offer, queue item, or persisted download record is created.
incidentTriage.escalateWhen: Unrelated clipboard content appears in state or diagnostics.

migrationGuidance.databaseMigration: Not applicable: v0.1 uses JSON sidecar manifests and local files; no database or infrastructure migration is required.
manifestChangeProcedure: Add an explicit schema version and keep the old reader or a separately tested converter.
Validate the source manifest before backup or conversion.
Write a temporary result, validate it, and replace atomically while retaining a recoverable prior copy until success.
Preserve URL, output identity, status, total bytes, segment boundaries, and completed offsets without promoting partial content.
Behaviorally test paused and recoverably interrupted records, invalid input, rollback, and byte-correct completion before release.
migrationGuidance.rollbackTrigger: Any parse error, invalid state or segment boundary, lost offset, path containment failure, completed/partial mismatch, or byte-integrity failure.
migrationGuidance.destructiveOperations: Do not delete user downloads or manifests as a migration step and do not perform destructive database operations.

traceability.limitation: The approved root GPL-3.0 LICENSE requirement is outside this workstream's allowed write paths and was reported missing by WS-09.

traceability.evidence: Controlled loopback runtime tests cover segmented 206 transfers, ignored-Range fallback, and byte equality.

traceability.limitation: Manifest restart classification and backup/restore are tested, but the current download function starts a new transfer and desktop pause/resume/cancel only changes an in-memory snapshot; end-to-end transfer control and restart continuation are not implemented.
Formatter runtime tests are not evidence of Windows WebView keyboard or screen-reader behavior; independent real-runtime UI verification remains required.
Sanitisation and collision behavior are shared, but reparse-point containment and trusted destination grants remain open security findings.
The offer is confirmation-based and non-URLs are ignored, but full accepted URLs are emitted and retained without a complete redaction/retention policy.

traceability.evidence: Windows Tauri is the only application topology; deferred platforms and capabilities have no delivery surface.
Shared transfer and persistence rules are owned by packages/download-engine and consumed by the Tauri adapter.

traceability.limitation: Only ENG-15 may issue the independent engineering disposition.

implementationNotes: This workstream changes technical documentation only and does not alter application behavior, dependencies, infrastructure, persistence schemas, or deployment state.
The Rust engine is a separate crate using tokio and reqwest and is consumed by the Tauri desktop crate.
Range fallback, filename safety, collision naming, manifest validation, backup/restore, restart classification, and metrics are implemented in the shared engine.
The current queue receives a queued and terminal snapshot but does not receive live per-segment progress events.

No analytics, AI, cloud service, web product, mobile product, browser extension, torrent, streaming capture, scheduler, bandwidth throttle, production deployment, signing, or public release is included.
knownRisks: Pause, resume, and cancel do not currently control the running engine task; restart recovery does not resume transfer bytes from persisted offsets.
Segment bodies are buffered in memory and requests have no explicit timeout or response-size cap.
Length-only integrity checks do not bind segments to a common strong validator, so a changing remote object can produce mixed content.
Full URLs, including query data, are persisted and emitted; redaction, access, retention, and cleanup policy is incomplete.
Destination strings are accepted from the webview and filesystem containment does not defend reparse-point races.
The queue lacks live progress, speed, and ETA updates during active transfers.
A root GPL-3.0 LICENSE, automated advisory scan, dependency-license evidence, signed installer evidence, and public distribution approval are not established by this workstream.
Windows WebView keyboard, screen-reader, clipboard, file-action, and full journey behavior still require independent runtime verification by ENG-15.
